per_finding.notes: The claim was removed from docs/RELEASE.md:153.
All 34 r2/r3 attack probes are caught (two were benign placeholders). All 11 known-good samples pass. The repo workflows pass: workflow-hardening rc=0 in 0.3 s.

issues.problem: A 'file' entry exempts the whole file from the identity-token check for good. graphify-out/graph.json (55 MB, regenerated after every code change) has exactly 1 legitimate identity line. The 7 other allowlisted files have 1 or 2 each, with 0 path-shaped uses. The only remaining detector of lowercase flattened home forms is the identity check, because FLAT_HOMES[0] is case-sensitive. So in graph.json a real users_<n>_..., -users-<n>-..., _home_<n>_..., ~<n>/ or a plain name mention is never reported. Lowercase flattened ids are the form graphify writes.
issues.evidence: pd4b.py: a temp repo with the real hash and allow files and an allowlisted graphify-out/graph.json. users_lower, dash_users_lower, home_lower_flat, tilde, tilde_slash and plain_name are MISSED in graph.json and CAUGHT in plain.txt. pd4c.py: the allowlisted files have 1-2 identity lines each and 0 path-shaped ones.
issues.suggested_fix: Report path-shaped identity tokens even in allowlisted files: (users|home)[-_/\\]+TOKEN or ~/?TOKEN, where TOKEN hashes to a listed token. This has no false positives, because only the maintainer's tokens match. Better still, make 'file' entries line-scoped, for example 'file <path> <sha256 of the allowed line>' or a maximum count, so that a new identity line in an allowlisted file fails.

issues.problem: The code-input key list misses common inputs that run as code, so untrusted ${{ }} passes in: azure/cli and azure/powershell inlineScript; cypress-io start, build and install-command; uraimo/run-on-arch install; gradle arguments; pre-command and post_run; a list-valued script:. Separately, container.options at job level is not checked.
issues.evidence: wf4new.py: azure_cli_inlineScript, azure_powershell_inlineScript, cypress_start, cypress_install_command, run_on_arch_install, gradle_arguments, pre_post_command, script_list_value and container_options are all MISSED. command, args, entrypoint, Script (any case) and the docker:// args are caught.
issues.suggested_fix: Flag untrusted contexts (github.event.*, github.head_ref, inputs.*, matrix values from fromJSON(event)) in any with: value, with an allowlist of known data inputs; or at least add inlinescript, start, build, install, install-command, arguments, pre-command, post-command and *-command / *_command patterns, and recurse into list values.

issues.problem: Not checked: pull_request_target or workflow_run combined with an actions/checkout of the head ref (the pwn-request pattern), and job permissions that grant write scopes other than write-all. 'uses: Actions/Checkout@v5' escapes the persist-credentials rule, because owner and repo in uses are case-insensitive. A reusable-workflow caller job (jobs.<id>.uses) is required to have timeout-minutes, a key GitHub does not allow on such jobs (false positive). None of the repo's workflows use these patterns today.
issues.evidence: wf4new.py: prt_checkout_head, workflow_run_artifact, perm_write_contents_job and checkout_upper are MISSED; reusable_call_with reports 'job a has no timeout-minutes'.
issues.suggested_fix: Fail on pull_request_target or workflow_run when a checkout has a ref: expression from github.event; match uses case-insensitively; skip the timeout-minutes rule for jobs with uses:.

issues.problem: Tokenizing raw bytes on non-alphanumerics misses a token glued to an escape or affix: a JSON-escaped newline or tab before a name ('\\n<Name> wrote', common in .json and .jsonl transcripts); %2F<n> and %20<n> outside a Users/ path (for example github.com%2F<n>%2Frepo, also missed by the home rule); \\u-escaped letters; &#NNN; letter entities; zero-width or soft-hyphen splits; NFKC or fullwidth forms and homoglyphs; concatenations such as <Name>Smith, <n>2 and 9<n>; base64 and hex. Case, every plain separator, /, /, / and markdown emphasis are caught.
issues.evidence: pd4.py, for both hashed tokens: json_newline, json_tab, json_u002f, json_u_letters, url_pct2F, url_pct20, html_letter_ent, zero_width, soft_hyphen, homoglyph, fullwidth, camel_concat, suffix_digit, prefix_digit, base64 and hex are all MISSED. pd4b.py: pct_users_only is MISSED even in non-allowlisted files.
issues.suggested_fix: Before tokenizing, decode JSON escapes (\\n, \\t, \\uXXXX), %XX and HTML numeric entities, apply NFKC and strip Cf characters, as the home rule already does for separators. Then also test each token's length-L prefix and suffix (L in the hash lengths), which is cheap and catches affixes and concatenations. Base64 and homoglyphs can stay a documented residual.

issues.problem: The hashes do not hide the identity. The 5-character token is recovered by plain [a-z] brute force in 14 s in pure Python. Both tokens are recovered in 8 ms by hashing the tokens of the allowlisted public file .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. The 7-character token is about 8e9 candidates, seconds on a GPU. This is acceptable only because the name is already public in the author fields; the hashes keep the literal out of the file, nothing more.
issues.evidence: pd4.py: 'dictionary attack from allowlisted public files recovered lengths [5, 7] in 0.008s'; 'brute force length-5 [a-z]: recovered=True after 9340300 candidates in 13.9s' (plaintext not printed).
issues.suggested_fix: State in the file header and in RELEASE.md that the hashes are obfuscation, not secrecy, and must never list a token that is not already public (for example a private second name or a private handle).

issues.problem: The delta removed docs/**/*-stdout.txt and docs/**/*-stderr.txt from .gitignore and added only docs/**/*.err. RELEASE.md still says that *-stdout.txt captures under docs/ are git-ignored. The tracked-file test still rejects committing them.
issues.evidence: git check-ignore: docs/a/review-stdout.txt and docs/a/b-stderr.txt are NOT-IGNORED.
issues.suggested_fix: Restore the two docs/** patterns, or fix the RELEASE.md sentence, and add docs/a/x-stdout.txt to the check-ignore loop in tests/scripts/test-no-personal-machine-paths.sh.

issues.problem: The validate job installs PyYAML into the runner's system python3 with no actions/setup-python, unlike the other jobs (ci.yml:109, :152). On ubuntu-latest (24.04) the system interpreter may be PEP 668 externally-managed, in which case pip fails. That would be loud, not silent, but it is unverified offline. The install is also unhashed.
issues.evidence: ci.yml validate steps: checkout, seed env, 'python3 -m pip install PyYAML==6.0.2', invariants. No setup-python step.
issues.suggested_fix: Add actions/setup-python@v6 (python 3.12) before the install, as the test jobs do, and confirm on a CI run.
